Job Summary

JOB DESCRIPTION

Works on research data reporting assignments that are of moderate diversity in scope. Exercises judgment within generally defined practices and policies in selecting methods and techniques for obtaining solutions. Involves gathering, analyzing, and interpreting a wide variety of research data. Designs and conducts research including selecting data samples, developing research instruments, analyzing collected information according to established statistical methods, and developing recommendations based on research findings. Prepares reports, charts, tables, and other visual aids to interpret and communicate data and results.

We are seeking a full-time Data Analyst to become an integral part of our team. We offer a positive environment with dedicated colleagues in the Department of Neurology at UCSF. The Research Data Analyst will support epidemiologic studies, which aim to collect data from people with Parkinson’s disease (PD), people at risk of developing PD, and other research volunteers to answer key scientific questions in the field.

The Research Data Analyst will be the primary analyst for an observational multicenter study Parkinson’s disease genetics study and will also participate in analyses of other related observational study datasets.

The Research Data Analyst will have the following responsibilities: 1) conduct primary statistical analyses, including data tabulation and reporting, descriptive statistics, and multivariate and longitudinal data analyses; 2) conduct data quality control 3) contribute to analyses of genetic risk factors for PD among ancestrally diverse samples. Secondary responsibilities include facilitating harmonization of study data with external datasets, interpreting and writing up results for publication, assisting with progress reports; and engaging in grant-writing process including preparation of preliminary analyses.

We are seeking a candidate who enjoys liaising with multiple study collaborators. The Research Data Analyst should show a strong interest in clinical research and a desire to contribute to the state of knowledge on genetics and other risk factors for Parkinson’s disease. The Research Data Analyst must be able to multi-task, problem-solve, and apply creative solutions to new and unexpected situations with limited supervision.

Department Description

The mission of the Department of Neurology at the University of California, San Francisco (UCSF) includes delivering the most exceptional clinical care to our patients, leading transformative cutting-edge research, and training the leaders of tomorrow in both neurology and neuroscience. Our department’s faculty, trainees, and staff work at a University and in a community that values and embraces diversity and strives to make an impact worldwide through our global and public health efforts.

We bring together expertise across planning, design, engineering, education and encouragement programs, and community engagement to help communities thrive. Our work is grounded in the belief that how places are designed and experienced has a profound impact on equity, health, and opportunity—and that people should always be at the heart of those decisions.

Metrea delivers effects-as-a-service to national security partners across five domains and more than a dozen mission areas. These include airborne ISR, electronic warfare, secure communications, aerial refuelling, special air missions, aerial firefighting, and advanced simulation. We own the whole stack: designing, building, and operating turnkey capabilities that give our partners decisive, asymmetric advantage against rapidly evolving threats.

Our operating model is built around three interlocking pillars. The Support Groups provide a global shared-service – spanning people, finance, platform, operations, legal, and engagement. This frees up our Core Groups, who develop and own mission capabilities end-to-end, to focus entirely on delivery. The Market Groups apply a regional lens, ensuring that our agile and adaptable capabilities remain aligned to the wicked problems that matter most to our partners across the Americas, EMEA, and Asia-Pacific.

At the heart of our model is a simple but powerful idea: be a true partner with skin in the game. Our partners need effects, not just equipment. By owning the full stack – from the lab to the field – we are able to drive a continuous cycle of innovation that keeps our partners ahead. It's a fast-moving, intellectually demanding environment where talented people are given real responsibility, work on problems that matter, and contribute to an enterprise that is growing quickly and deliberately.

Experience integrating metadata and multi-source contexts to raise analytic confidence.
Experience with conducting SI collection operations, including system operating familiarity
Strong writing skills for time-sensitive reporting and analytic notes.
Familiarity with RF environments (cellular/Wi‑Fi/radios) and emitter characterization preferred.
Comfort working with data tables, identifiers, and link analysis concepts.
Ability to brief findings and answer RFIs in fast-paced operations.
Highly collaborative and able to build strong relationships with technical experts.
Detail-oriented with an ability to effectively contribute to multiple projects, with a focus on quality, on-time deliverables.
Comfortable working in fast-paced, multi-disciplinary environments.
Curious, adaptable, and willing to learn new concepts and subjects to communicate those effectively.

Description

As the largest and oldest department within the UC San Diego School of Medicine, the Department of Medicine employs nearly 500 faculty members and 1,000 academic appointees, residents, fellows, postdocs, and staff, in pursuit of its academic, clinical, and research missions.

The Division of Gastroenterology and Hepatology in the Department of Medicine conducts research studies which study Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) in adult patients. The MASLD Research Center focus on the etiology, contributing factors, natural history, complications, and therapy of MASH and MASLD. The MASLD Research Center participates in pharmaceutical clinical trials and Principal Investigator (PI) initiated studies which focus on the discovery and validation of innovative biomarkers for MASLD, with a special focus on identifying those patients at greatest risk for MASH, advanced liver fibrosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC).

Under general supervision, uses multiple statistical software packages to look for outliers and anomalies in the data. Alta Planning + Design seeks a Civic Data Analyst (Sustainable Mobility)

About Alta

Alta is a mission-driven company working to mitigate climate change and advance safety and social justice by shaping sustainable, people-centered communities. We bring together expertise across planning, design, engineering, education and encouragement programs, and community engagement to help communities thrive. Our work is grounded in the belief that how places are designed and experienced has a profound impact on equity, health, and opportunity—and that people should always be at the heart of those decisions.

Founded in 1996, Alta was at the forefront of the active transportation movement and has spent nearly 30 years partnering with communities to imagine a more connected, resilient, and inclusive future. Today, with more than 225 staff across the United States and beyond, we are a global leader in creating environments that support everyday life, strengthen human connection, and respond to the challenges of a changing world. Alta offers the opportunity to collaborate across disciplines, contribute to meaningful work at every scale, and be part of a team committed to making lasting, positive change for people and the places they call home.

Day to Day

Serve as a technical expert and analyst across various disciplines, project types, and regions. Develop prototypes of repeatable analysis in R, Python, and GIS to advance place-based sustainable transportation solutions. Over time, foster an entrepreneurial approach to analysis through staff training, research, tool development, and custom web applications.

Engage across Alta’s disciplines to understand data analytics needs, priorities, and expectations, fostering a data-informed decision-making culture. Lead the development of new analytical products that align with the firm's objectives and the multidisciplinary nature of the practice. Collaborate closely with planners, designers, and engineers in tasks related to data analysis and visualization, ensuring the developed solutions bring valuable mobility insights and can scale organization wide.

Delve into data analysis and visualization components of client projects and R&D efforts, employing complex methodologies. Address mobility and access challenges through innovative analytical solutions, and articulate data-driven narratives effectively through reports, technical memos, and presentations. Be proactive in identifying labor-intensive processes and analysis, exploring avenues to streamline and automate them to create organization-wide value Work on a range of projects including active transportation plans, safety action plans, complete streets planning, safe routes to school, new mobility plans, and economic benefit studies. Each day, you will keep a community-focused perspective by pushing forward solutions that help communities inform narratives about people, address multifaceted community goals, prepare communities for change, and build a more just transportation system.

Qualifications

Required

This position requires a combination of skills, experience and education including, but not limited to Bachelor’s Degree in Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science or another quantitative field with demonstrated experience in the transportation planning field, OR a Bachelor’s Degree in Planning, Landscape Architecture, Environmental Sciences, or Engineering with some experience in the software development and/or data science fields.
Proficiency in Python and/or R, SQL

Proficiency in Quantitative Analysis:
A solid background in data analysis, cross tabulation, and data interpretation is essential. Candidates should be able to apply data driven techniques to inform evidence-based decision-making in planning and design contexts.
Strong understanding of databases, GIS, coding, and familiarity with transportation planning at an advanced level.
GIS Proficiency - both open-source (PostGIS, QGIS, geopandas, etc.) and the ESRI suite (ArcGISPro, Spatial Analyst, Network Analyst, etc.).
Ability to create informative data visualizations through code (e.g. D3, ggplot, matplotlib, plotly, kepler.gl, etc.).
Experience designing, implementing, and documenting analytical solutions using code. Ability to execute an analysis entirely with code.
Data specifications & database acronyms like OSM, MDS, GTFS, GBFS, GPS, CDS don’t scare you.
Proficient in MS Excel, Word, PowerPoint, similar products.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.

Preferred
There are a number of additional skills, experience, and education that would be beneficial to this position including, but not limited to: Master’s Degree in Urban Planning, Statistics, Data Science, Engineering, Math, or Social Sciences
1+ years of experience in a consulting environment or public entity. You have experience working on responses to public sector requests for proposals.
AICP Certification.
Experience using Deltek VantagePoint.
Active participation in industry-relevant professional associations and committees.
Demonstrated work of applied statistics or machine learning techniques to transportation challenges.
Basic familiarity with deploying analytical solutions over the web with the use of Flask, Django, Fast-API, Tableau, PowerBI, ArcGIS Enterprise, or R-Shiny.

Flexible Schedule

Alta offers a flexible, hybrid work schedule where most employees work from home three days per week. In-office days support our collaborative culture, one of our core values.

annually. Placement within the range is based upon experience, skill-sets, and qualifications.

Role Overview

JOB DESCRIPTION

As Project Coordinator, Special Projects, you will support construction-focused data center projects by coordinating schedules, action tracking, documentation, meetings, and cross-functional follow-through. This role helps Special Projects teams execute remediation, retrofit, expansion, and infrastructure improvement work with clear visibility, disciplined records, and timely issue resolution.

You will partner with project managers, construction managers, engineering teams, commissioning partners, site operations, procurement, vendors, and technical SMEs. The role requires strong organization, communication, document control, and project tracking skills in active mission-critical environments.

Responsibilities

Key Responsibilities

Support project managers and technical leads in coordinating Special Projects construction activities across assigned sites or workstreams.
Maintain project schedules, action registers, meeting notes, issue logs, risk trackers, decision logs, and documentation repositories.
Coordinate meetings, agendas, follow-ups, owner assignments, and status updates with internal teams, contractors, vendors, and site stakeholders.
Track submittals, closeout documents, commissioning evidence, punch lists, turnover requirements, and operational handoff materials.
Support readiness reviews by gathering updates from Construction, Engineering, Operations, Commissioning, Procurement, and vendors.
Prepare concise project status summaries, milestone updates, blocker reports, and leadership-ready action lists.
Monitor open items to ensure accountable owners, due dates, dependencies, and escalation paths remain clear.
Assist with procurement tracking, vendor coordination, access requests, logistics, site visit planning, and document routing.
Help ensure project records support audit readiness, warranty tracking, asset onboarding, safety expectations, and handoff discipline.
Identify recurring process gaps and recommend improvements to templates, trackers, meeting cadence, and documentation standards.
Support multiple concurrent projects while maintaining accurate records and timely communication.
Reinforce safety, access-control , and active-site protocols when coordinating project activities.

Ideal Candidate Profile

5+ years of experience in project coordination, construction administration, data center support, facilities operations, engineering support, procurement coordination, or technical program support.
Experience coordinating projects in construction, mission-critical facilities, data centers, utilities, industrial operations, or infrastructure environments.
Strong ability to maintain trackers, schedules, action logs, meeting notes, and document repositories.
Experience working with project managers, contractors, vendors, engineering teams, and site operations stakeholders.
Strong written communication, follow-up discipline, and attention to detail.
Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience in construction management, business, operations, engineering, or a related field.

Skills And Competencies

Excellent organization and project tracking discipline.
Clear communication with strong follow- through on actions, owners, and due dates.
Ability to manage competing priorities across multiple projects.
Comfort working with technical teams and translating updates into clear project records.
Strong document control mindset with attention to versioning, completeness, and auditability.
Collaborative approach to supporting project execution in active data center environments.

Preferred Skills / Certifications

Experience with Smartsheet, MS Project, Primavera, Procore, Jira, SharePoint, CMMS, or document control systems.
Familiarity with construction closeout, commissioning, punch lists, O&M; documentation, as-builts, warranties, and turnover packages.
CAPM, PMP, OSHA, construction management, document control, or project coordination certification.
Experience supporting hyperscale data centers, colocation, utilities, critical manufacturing, or other mission-critical environments.
Working knowledge of data center power, cooling, controls, security, and operational readiness concepts.

This role operates across office, remote collaboration, construction, commissioning, and active data center environments. The position may require travel to sites. Site visits may involve walking large facilities, standing for extended periods, using stairs, and following all safety, PPE, security, and access-control requirements.
